checks.explanation: Tim Walz has remained a visible if lower-profile figure as Minnesota governor; no sustained SNL running-gag about his forgettability specifically materialized, though he did not become a major national figure post-election.
The predicted 8-year window (through 2032) has not elapsed, so whether Democrats lose California or New York cannot yet be judged.
The Democratic Party has visibly debated and shifted toward more centrist messaging and candidates in the cycles following the 2024 defeat.
There were no Capitol-style riots or large-scale violent mob attacks on police following Trump's 2024 election victory; the transition was peaceful.
The final 2024 Senate count settled at 53 Republican seats, not the 54 predicted.
Robert F. Kennedy Jr. was successfully confirmed as Secretary of Health and Human Services in February 2025 under the 53-seat Republican majority.
Trump did not end the Ukraine war on his first day in office; the conflict continued well into 2025 and 2026 without a finalized peace deal.
Congress did not enact anything close to $2 trillion in federal spending cuts; DOGE's realized savings fell far short of that target.

Some transparency and declassification efforts occurred (e.g., JFK files, attempts at Epstein-related disclosures), but no comprehensive 'Twitter files for the government' style release program was carried out as described.

Remaining JFK assassination files were declassified in 2025, but the Epstein files release became a major, unresolved political controversy with only partial disclosure, and no significant 'dirty lists' were made public.
Some declassification occurred (notably JFK files) but not the broad sweeping release of federal information across the board that was predicted.
A large-scale declassification program substantially reducing classified federal document volume has not been clearly documented; only targeted releases occurred.
Reducing the autonomy of the federal bureaucracy and increasing executive control (via DOGE and related restructuring efforts) became a defining, central theme of Trump's second term.
This is a 20-year historical characterization that cannot be assessed only a couple of years into the predicted era.
David Sacks instead took a role in the Trump administration as AI and crypto czar rather than running for California governor.
With Sacks serving in the Trump administration as of 2026 and no indication of a gubernatorial campaign, this prediction did not come to pass within the stated roughly two-year window.
The Democratic Party has shown a visible centrist shift in strategy and messaging in the years following the 2024 election, consistent with this prediction.
Abortion has remained a significant issue in various state-level elections and ballot measures since 2024, so it has not clearly faded as a national wedge issue as predicted.
Republican leaders, including the Trump administration, have largely avoided pushing for a national abortion ban, leaving the issue primarily at the state level.
No such hypothetical 15-week Florida abortion referendum has been put to voters to test this specific claim.

While some anecdotal and survey evidence suggests migration considerations tied to abortion policy, a clear, isolated out-migration effect specifically attributable to abortion bans has not been definitively established.
